items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: He used to buy this big Victor Red Seal records with Alma Gluck and Madame Tettrazini and Schumann-Heinck

ctx.x: Yeah. And so then they shifted over. Every now and then they'd have an article about who was playing then and all the -- you know, then I realized that it was -- then by the time I got to -- I remember distinctly, by the time I go to the National School on 116th Street, you know, I was about 18 years old by then I guess. 18 or 17 or 18. Then I remember the first -- I don't remember who wrote the article and I don't remember what publication it was in, but I remember

somebody came down on Fletcher Henderson's band, and it said something about the band didn't sound good, or they didn't care what they were playing or something along that order, you know. Then I realized, oh, somebody's paying attention, you know. And this was real early, early in my career, you know. But music -- so at first I did realize that it was just part of the whole music scene, you know, because I -- that old Victrola at home that I've got, that my father used to buy these records. He used to buy this…
And of course much later you were doing a lot of classical music with Kirby, right?
